title: Congo Free State
capsule: The Congo Free State (État indépendant du Congo, 1885–1908) was the personal property of King Leopold II of Belgium, recognized by the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 on his claim of bringing free trade and civilizing missions to Central Africa. In practice, a system of forced rubber and ivory extraction, enforced by the Force Publique through hostage-taking, mutilation, and massacre, killed an estimated two to ten million Congolese. The international reform campaign led by E.D. Morel, Roger Casement's 1904 consular report, and relentless pressure from humanitarians and foreign governments forced Leopold to cede the territory to the Belgian state on 15 November 1908, when it became the Belgian Congo.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The external boundaries of the Congo Free State are well-documented from the Berlin Act (1885) and subsequent treaties; internal administrative divisions are less precisely mapped.
